angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 751,356 km at 177.35 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6384 +/- 0.0143 mas (same row, RUWE 0.84): 177.35 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.08 +/- 0.06 solar radii from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of BD+20 594 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract): 751,356 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.67 +/- 0.4 solar masses from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of BD+20 594 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5766 +/- 99 K from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of BD+20 594 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of BD+20 594 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/bd-20-594.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.594, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
